newsitem.title: UK: Eurobourses mixed, dollar slightly softer.
newsitem.headline: Eurobourses mixed, dollar slightly softer.

text.p: European shares traded mixed on Monday morning as Friday's uninspiring close on Wall Street weighed on sentiment and dealers said currency markets were also quiet, lacking incentive before key U.S. data this week.

London shares were down about a third of a percentage point by late morning, influenced by a batch of heavyweight stocks going ex-dividend and with sentiment nervous after Friday's New York trading, which ended with the Dow just a few points up.
Dealers said the fact that Barclays and Lloyds TSB were both trading ex their declared dividends was pulling the market lower.

Investors were also concerned that the strength of sterling -- at its highest level since it left the European exchange rate mechanism in 1992 -- would affect earnings as the corporate results season gets fully under way.
In Frankfurt, German shares moved into positive territory after starting lower but dealers said sentiment was still weighed on by the softening of the dollar -- which is negative for German exports.
In Paris, too, shares found some buying support and showed narrow gains in early trading.

Traders said the market was supported by buying on the first account day although it was trading under the sway of softer domestic and German bonds, the retracement of the dollar and New York's mixed close last Friday.

One focus on the Paris bourse was loss-making Club Mediterranee , which surged almost 17 percent, after being suspended limit up twice during the morning, on positive perceptions of its new chairman, former Euro Disney head Philippe Bourguignon.

Both equities and currency markets were treading water to an extent ahead of U.S. Federal Reserve Chairman Alan Greenspan's semi-annual commentary on the U.S. economy to Senate and House committees on Wednesday and Thursday.
His utterances will, as usual, be scrutinized for clues to future U.S. credit policy.
On currency markets, traders said the dollar was softening marginally against the mark and yen and by late morning it was just above session lows at around 122 yen and 1.6750 marks.

"We'll probably see some range trading today. With such important things coming up this week, people don't want to start taking very aggressive positions," said Thomas Rayner, international economist at Societe Generale Strauss Turnbull.

"We tend to think Mr. Greenspan will raise again some fears about the labour market and the potential for inflation. If he does, the market is going to start factoring in an early rate hike and this should push the dollar to the 1.70 level (to the mark)," he added.
Economic data showing signs of some health in the German economy last week was also making the market wary of being too long on the dollar and giving it a softer tone, analysts said.

Also weighing on the dollar was a Washington Post article on Sunday which quoted sources as saying some senior U.S. officials expressed concern about the U.S. stock market, saying "the higher the market goes, the closer it could be to a correction".
Analysts said this report was causing worries, particularly ahead of Fed chairman Alan Greenspan's Humphrey Hawkins testimony.
CURRENCIES AT 1145 GMT
The dollar was quoted at 1.6750 marks and 122.00 yen, compared with 1.6883 and 123.20 in late European trade on Friday.
STOCK MARKETS AT 1145 GMT
LONDON - The FTSE-100 index was down 15.8 points at 4,321.0.
PARIS - The CAC-40 was up 10.1 points at 2,572.94.
FRANKFURT - The 30-share DAX index was up 1.8 points at 3,185.89.
PRECIOUS METALS
Gold fixed at $352.45, compared with $353.75 at the London close on Friday.
